name: XGBoost (eXtreme Gradient Boosting)
description: XGBoost is an optimized, distributed gradient boosting library designed for speed and performance. It adds regularization to standard gradient boosting, supports parallel processing, and includes built-in cross-validation and missing value handling. It's one of the most popular algorithms for structured data competitions.

concept.objectiveFunction: Obj = Loss + Regularization = Σl(yᵢ, ŷᵢ) + ΣΩ(fₖ)
concept.regularization: Ω(f) = γT + ½λΣw² where T=leaves, w=leaf weights
concept.approximation: Second-order Taylor expansion of loss function
concept.splitFinding: Greedy algorithm with exact or approximate (histogram) methods
concept.explanation: XGBoost optimizes both training loss and model complexity (number of leaves and leaf weights). Uses second derivatives (Hessian) for more accurate optimization. Supports column and row subsampling.

maxDepth.impact: Higher = more complex model, risk of overfitting

learningRate.impact: Lower = more robust to overfitting, need more trees

nEstimators.impact: More trees with lower learning rate = better generalization

minChildWeight.description: Minimum sum of instance weight in child
minChildWeight.impact: Controls tree complexity; higher = more conservative

preprocessing: XGBoost handles missing values internally (set as np.nan)
Categorical features need encoding (one-hot or target encoding)
tuningStrategy: Step 1: Fix high learning_rate (0.1), tune n_estimators with early stopping
Step 5: Lower learning_rate, increase n_estimators proportionally

complexity.timeTraining: O(n × p × log(n) × n_estimators) with optimizations

cons: Memory intensive for very large models

uniqueFeatures.monotonicConstraints: Enforce monotonic relationships between features and output

resources.paper: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
